newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's FIS calls on army for support.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's FIS calls on army for support.

text.p: Algeria's banned Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) called on the country's army on Sunday to turn against their own commanders who have locked them in bloody confrontation with FIS and other armed fundamentalist groups.

"We call on the soldiers and officers of the Algerian army to express their rejection of the policy of confrontation and blood-letting among Algerians and their preference for a peaceful solution," said a statement by the group's European branch.
It said such a stance by the army "will serve the army and the people's interests because it alone will enable an end to the bloodshed."
The statement, sent to a news agency in Paris, was issued to mark the fifth anniversary of the cancellation by Algerian military chiefs of elections the fundamentalists appeared poised to win.
The move sparked a civil war which FIS said had claimed 120,000 lives and forced 60,000 people to flee the country.

The statement said army claims to be winning the war against Islamic guerrillas, including the extremist Armed Islamic Group (GIA), were belied by an upsurge in bomb attacks in Algeria's cities which killed dozens of people in recent weeks.
FIS condemned the bombings which it described as abominable, implying it was blaming them on the rival GIA.
